title: Forgive my mistakes, my ignorance and my excess
narrator: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي خَطِيئَتِي وَجَهْلِي وَإِسْرَافِي فِي أَمْرِي وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي جِدِّي وَهَزْلِي وَخَطَئِي وَعَمْدِي وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ عِنْدِي اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
transliteration: Allahummaghfir li khati'ati wa jahli wa israfi fi amri wa ma anta a'lamu bihi minni. Allahummaghfir li jiddi wa hazli wa khata'i wa 'amdi, wa kullu dhalika 'indi. Allahummaghfir li ma qaddamtu wa ma akhkhart, wa ma asrartu wa ma a'lant, wa ma anta a'lamu bihi minni. Antal-muqaddimu wa antal-mu'akhkhir, wa anta 'ala kulli shay'in qadir.
english_translation: O Allah, forgive me my mistakes, my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and what You know better than I do. O Allah, forgive me what I did in earnest and in jest, in error and on purpose, and all of that is in me. O Allah, forgive me what I sent ahead and what I left behind, what I concealed and what I made known, and what You know better than I do. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back, and You have power over all things.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Meri ghaltiyan, meri jahalat, apne kaam mein meri ziyadatiyan aur woh sab jo tu mujh se ziyada jaanta hai, maaf farma de. Ae Allah! Meri sanjeedagi aur mazaq, meri bhool aur jaan boojh kar ki hui baatein bakhsh de, aur yeh sab mujh mein hai. Ae Allah! Jo maine aage bheja aur jo peechhe chhoda, jo chhupa kar kiya aur jo zahir kiya aur jo tu mujh se ziyada jaanta hai, bakhsh de. Tu hi aage karne wala aur tu hi peechhe karne wala hai aur tu har cheez par qadir hai.
explanation: A comprehensive request for forgiveness that covers every kind of fault, including those one is unaware of.
wording_note: Slightly different wordings of this supplication are reported in Sahih al-Bukhari (6398–6399). This text follows Sahih Muslim 2719.
context: Abu Musa reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to make this supplication.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي خَطِيئَتِي وَجَهْلِي وَإِسْرَافِي فِي أَمْرِي وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي جِدِّي وَهَزْلِي وَخَطَئِي وَعَمْدِي وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ عِنْدِي اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

title: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live
narrator: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
transliteration: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya.
english_translation: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Tere hi naam ke saath main marta hoon aur jeeta hoon.
explanation: Said when going to bed, entrusting sleep and waking to Allah.
context: Hudhayfah reported that when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed at night he would place his hand under his cheek and say this.
arabic_parts: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die
narrator: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
transliteration: Alhamdu lillahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.
english_translation: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He made us die, and to Him is the resurrection.
roman_urdu_translation: Tamam tareef Allah ke liye jis ne hamein maut (neend) ke baad zindagi bakhshi aur usi ki taraf uth kar jaana hai.
explanation: Thanks Allah for waking, comparing sleep to a small death.
context: Hudhayfah reported that the Prophet ﷺ would say this when he woke from sleep.
arabic_parts: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: I have submitted myself to You
narrator: al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ، وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ، وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ، رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ، لاَ مَلْجَأَ وَلاَ مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلاَّ إِلَيْكَ، اللَّهُمَّ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ، وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ‏.‏
transliteration: Allahumma aslamtu wajhi ilayk, wa fawwadtu amri ilayk, wa alja'tu zahri ilayk, raghbatan wa rahbatan ilayk. La malja'a wa la manja minka illa ilayk. Allahumma amantu bikitabikal-ladhi anzalt, wa binabiyyikal-ladhi arsalt.
english_translation: O Allah, I have submitted my face (my whole self) to You, entrusted my affair to You, and turned my back to You for support, in hope and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down and in Your Prophet whom You sent.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Maine apna chehra (apni poori zaat) tere hawale kar diya, apna kaam tujhe soump diya aur apni pusht teri taraf tikka di, teri ummeed aur tere khauf ke saath. Tujh se bachne ki koi jagah aur koi panah nahin magar teri hi taraf. Ae Allah! Main tere us kitab par iman laya jo tu ne utari aur tere us nabi par jise tu ne bheja.
explanation: Hands over every concern to Allah, in both hope and fear, and affirms belief in the Quran and the Prophet ﷺ.
wording_note: Narrations differ slightly; for example another narration in Sahih al-Bukhari has 'aslamtu nafsi' (I have submitted myself). This text follows Sahih al-Bukhari 247.
context: Al-Bara' reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught him to say this when going to bed.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ، وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ، وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ، رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ، لاَ مَلْجَأَ وَلاَ مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلاَّ إِلَيْكَ، اللَّهُمَّ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ، وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ‏.‏

title: Settle our debts and enrich us from poverty
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَرَبَّ الأَرْضِ وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ رَبَّنَا وَرَبَّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ فَالِقَ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى وَمُنْزِلَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَالإِنْجِيلِ وَالْفُرْقَانِ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ أَنْتَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهِ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَىْءٌ اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
transliteration: Allahumma rabbas-samawati wa rabbal-ardi wa rabbal-'arshil-'azim, rabbana wa rabba kulli shay', faliqal-habbi wan-nawa, wa munzilat-tawrati wal-injili wal-furqan. A'udhu bika min sharri kulli shay'in anta akhidhun binasiyatih. Allahumma antal-awwalu falaysa qablaka shay', wa antal-akhiru falaysa ba'daka shay', wa antaz-zahiru falaysa fawqaka shay', wa antal-batinu falaysa dunaka shay'. Iqdi 'annad-dayna wa aghnina minal-faqr.
english_translation: O Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of everything, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion. I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First, nothing is before You; You are the Last, nothing is after You; You are the Manifest, nothing is above You; and You are the Hidden, nothing is beyond You. Settle our debts for us and enrich us from poverty.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Aasmanon ke Rab, zameen ke Rab aur azeem arsh ke Rab, hamare Rab aur har cheez ke Rab, daane aur guthli ko phaarne wale, Taurat, Injeel aur Furqan utarne wale! Main teri panah mangta hoon har us cheez ke shar se jis ki peshani tere qabze mein hai. Ae Allah! Tu hi awwal hai, tujh se pehle kuchh nahin; tu hi aakhir hai, tere baad kuchh nahin; tu hi zahir hai, tere upar kuchh nahin; aur tu hi batin hai, tere siwa kuchh nahin. Hamara qarz ada kara de aur hamein muhtaji se be-niyaz kar de.
explanation: Begins with Allah's names and attributes, then asks for refuge, relief from debt, and freedom from poverty.
context: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught this to say when going to bed, lying on the right side.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَرَبَّ الأَرْضِ وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ رَبَّنَا وَرَبَّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ فَالِقَ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوَى وَمُنْزِلَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَالإِنْجِيلِ وَالْفُرْقَانِ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ أَنْتَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهِ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَىْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَىْءٌ اقْضِ عَنَّا الدَّيْنَ وَأَغْنِنَا مِنَ الْفَقْرِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: When calamity strikes: we belong to Allah
narrator: Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her)
arabic: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
transliteration: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un. Allahumma'jurni fi musibati wa akhlif li khayran minha.
english_translation: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it for me with something better.
roman_urdu_translation: Hum Allah ke hain aur usi ki taraf lautne wale hain. Ae Allah! Meri is museebat mein mujhe ajar de aur is ke badle mein mujhe is se behtar ata farma.
explanation: Declares that everything belongs to Allah, then asks for reward in the loss and something better in return.
context: Umm Salamah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever is struck by a calamity and says this will have Allah replace it with something better. She said it after the death of Abu Salamah.
arabic_parts: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Seeking refuge in Allah's perfect words — as the Prophet ﷺ did for al-Hasan and al-Husayn
narrator: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ
transliteration: A'udhu bikalimatillahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammatin wa min kulli 'aynin lammah.
english_translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every harmful creature, and from every evil eye.
roman_urdu_translation: Main Allah ke mukammal kalimaat ki panah mangta hoon har shaitan se, har zehreele jandar se aur har lagne wali buri nazar se.
explanation: The words the Prophet ﷺ used when seeking Allah's protection for his grandsons. Parents often recite them over their children.
context: Ibn 'Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to seek protection for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, saying that their forefather Ibrahim used to seek protection for Isma'il and Ishaq with these words.
wording_note: Other narrations outside this collection use the form 'u'idhukuma' (I seek refuge for you both). This text follows Sahih al-Bukhari 3371.
arabic_parts: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah
narrator: Khawlah bint Hakim (may Allah be pleased with her)
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
transliteration: A'udhu bikalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.
english_translation: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
roman_urdu_translation: Main Allah ke mukammal kalimaat ki panah mangta hoon us ke shar se jo usne paida kiya.
explanation: A short request for Allah's protection, taught for when one stops somewhere on a journey.
context: Khawlah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever stops at a place and says this, nothing will harm him until he leaves that place. Protection remains in Allah's hands.
arabic_parts: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Remove the harm, Lord of mankind, and heal
narrator: 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
arabic: أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، اشْفِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِي لاَ شِفَاءَ إِلاَّ شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لاَ يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
transliteration: Adhhibil-ba's rabban-nas, ishfi wa antash-shafi, la shifa'a illa shifa'uk, shifa'an la yughadiru saqama.
english_translation: Remove the harm, Lord of mankind, and heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing — a healing that leaves no illness behind.
roman_urdu_translation: Takleef door kar de, ae logon ke Rab, aur shifa de, kyunke tu hi shifa dene wala hai. Teri shifa ke siwa koi shifa nahin, aisi shifa jo koi bimari baaqi na chhode.
explanation: Asks Allah for healing while acknowledging that all healing comes from Him.
wording_note: Wording differs slightly between narrations (for example 'ishfihi' and 'washfi anta ash-shafi'). This text follows Sahih al-Bukhari 5675.
context: 'A'ishah reported that the Prophet ﷺ would say this when he visited a sick person or when one was brought to him.
arabic_parts: أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، اشْفِ وَأَنْتَ الشَّافِي لاَ شِفَاءَ إِلاَّ شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لاَ يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: For pain in the body: place a hand on the spot
narrator: 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ
transliteration: Bismillah (three times). A'udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhir (seven times).
english_translation: In the name of Allah (three times). I seek refuge in Allah and in His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear (seven times).
roman_urdu_translation: Allah ke naam se (teen baar). Main Allah ki aur uski qudrat ki panah mangta hoon us takleef ke shar se jo main mehsoos karta hoon aur jis se darta hoon (saat baar).
explanation: Taught for bodily pain: place the hand on the place of pain and recite as described.
repetition_note: The narration says to say 'Bismillah' three times, then the second part seven times.
context: 'Uthman complained to the Prophet ﷺ of a pain he had had since he became Muslim, and the Prophet ﷺ taught him this.
arabic_parts: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ وَقُدْرَتِهِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ وَأُحَاذِرُ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Refuge from the loss of Your blessings and of well-being
narrator: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَوَالِ نِعْمَتِكَ وَتَحَوُّلِ عَافِيَتِكَ وَفُجَاءَةِ نِقْمَتِكَ وَجَمِيعِ سَخَطِكَ
transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min zawali ni'matik, wa tahawwuli 'afiyatik, wa fuja'ati niqmatik, wa jami'i sakhatik.
english_translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the removal of Your blessing, the change of the well-being You gave, the suddenness of Your punishment, and all of Your displeasure.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Main teri panah mangta hoon teri naimat ke chhin jane se, teri di hui afiyat ke badal jane se, teri achanak pakad se aur tere har qism ke ghussay se.
explanation: Asks Allah to preserve the blessings and well-being one already has.
context: Ibn 'Umar reported that this was among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَوَالِ نِعْمَتِكَ وَتَحَوُّلِ عَافِيَتِكَ وَفُجَاءَةِ نِقْمَتِكَ وَجَمِيعِ سَخَطِكَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: After eating: abundant, good and blessed praise
narrator: Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ، غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ، وَلاَ مُوَدَّعٍ وَلاَ مُسْتَغْنًى عَنْهُ، رَبَّنَا
transliteration: Alhamdu lillahi kathiran tayyiban mubarakan fihi, ghayra makfiyyin wa la muwadda'in wa la mustaghnan 'anhu rabbana.
english_translation: Praise be to Allah, abundantly — good and blessed praise; a praise that is never enough, never abandoned, and never dispensed with, our Lord.
roman_urdu_translation: Allah ki bohat sari, pakeeza aur barkat wali tareef, aisi tareef jo kabhi kaafi nahin hoti, jise chhoda nahin ja sakta aur jis se be-niyaz nahin hua ja sakta, ae hamare Rab!
explanation: Thanks Allah after finishing a meal.
context: Abu Umamah reported that when the Prophet ﷺ's food was lifted, he would say this.
arabic_parts: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ، غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ، وَلاَ مُوَدَّعٍ وَلاَ مُسْتَغْنًى عَنْهُ، رَبَّنَا
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Before eating: mention the name of Allah
narrator: 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: سَمِّ اللَّهَ، وَكُلْ بِيَمِينِكَ وَكُلْ مِمَّا يَلِيكَ
transliteration: Sammillah, wa kul biyaminik, wa kul mimma yalik.
english_translation: Mention Allah's name, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.
roman_urdu_translation: Allah ka naam lo (Bismillah kaho), seedhe haath se khao aur apne saamne se khao.
explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ words to a child about the etiquette of eating, beginning with the name of Allah (saying 'Bismillah').
context: The Prophet ﷺ said this to 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who was a boy in his care, when his hand moved around the dish.
arabic_parts: سَمِّ اللَّهَ، وَكُلْ بِيَمِينِكَ وَكُلْ مِمَّا يَلِيكَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: The supplication of travel
narrator: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic:
سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
آيِبُونَ تَائِبُونَ عَابِدُونَ لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
transliteration:
(Say 'Allahu akbar' three times, then:) Subhanal-ladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila rabbina lamunqalibun. Allahumma inna nas'aluka fi safarina hadhal-birra wat-taqwa, wa minal-'amali ma tarda. Allahumma hawwin 'alayna safarana hadha watwi 'anna bu'dah. Allahumma antas-sahibu fis-safar, wal-khalifatu fil-ahl. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'tha'is-safar, wa ka'abatil-manzar, wa su'il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahl.
(On returning, add:) Ayibuna ta'ibuna 'abiduna lirabbina hamidun.
english_translation:
(Allah is the Greatest, three times, then:) Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, though we could never have subdued it ourselves, and indeed to our Lord we will return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and for deeds that please You. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance for us. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian of the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a sorrowful sight, and from a bad return in wealth and family. (On returning, add:) We return, repentant, worshipping, and praising our Lord.
(On returning, add:) We return, repentant, worshipping, and praising our Lord.
roman_urdu_translation:
(Allah sab se bada hai, teen baar, phir:) Paak hai woh jis ne is sawari ko hamare qabu mein kar diya, hum ise qabu mein karne wale na the, aur hum apne Rab ki taraf lautne wale hain. Ae Allah! Hum apne is safar mein tujh se neki aur parhezgari ka sawal karte hain aur aise amal ka jis se tu razi ho. Ae Allah! Hamare liye yeh safar aasan kar de aur iski doori lapet de. Ae Allah! Tu safar mein saathi aur ahl o ayal mein nigehbaan hai. Ae Allah! Main teri panah mangta hoon safar ki mushaqqat se, bure manzar se aur maal aur ahl o ayal mein bure lautne se. (Wapsi par yeh izafa karo:) Hum lautne wale hain, tauba karne wale, ibadat karne wale aur apne Rab ki hamd karne wale.
(Wapsi par yeh izafa karo:) Hum lautne wale hain, tauba karne wale, ibadat karne wale aur apne Rab ki tareef karne wale.
explanation: Recited at the start of a journey: it glorifies Allah, asks for righteousness and ease, and asks Him to look after one's family.
context: Ibn 'Umar reported that when the Prophet ﷺ mounted his camel to set out on a journey, he would say 'Allahu akbar' three times, then say this. When he returned, he said the same and added the closing words.
arabic_parts: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالأَهْلِ
آيِبُونَ تَائِبُونَ عَابِدُونَ لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Entering the mosque: open the doors of Your mercy
narrator: Abu Humayd or Abu Usayd (may Allah be pleased with them)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
transliteration: Allahummaf-tah li abwaba rahmatik.
english_translation: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Mere liye apni rehmat ke darwaze khol de.
explanation: Said when entering the mosque.
context: The Prophet ﷺ said: when one of you enters the mosque, let him say this.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Leaving the mosque: I ask You for Your bounty
narrator: Abu Humayd or Abu Usayd (may Allah be pleased with them)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.
english_translation: O Allah, I ask You for Your bounty.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Main tujh se tere fazl ka sawal karta hoon.
explanation: Said when leaving the mosque, asking Allah for His bounty.
context: The Prophet ﷺ said: when one of you leaves, let him say this.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: After the prayer: seek forgiveness three times
narrator: Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
transliteration: Astaghfirullah.
english_translation: I seek forgiveness from Allah.
roman_urdu_translation: Main Allah se maafi mangta hoon.
explanation: The first thing the Prophet ﷺ said after finishing the prayer.
repetition_note: Thawban reported that when the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer he would seek forgiveness three times.
context: Thawban reported that when the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer he would say 'Astaghfirullah' three times.
arabic_parts: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: O Allah, You are Peace and from You is peace
narrator: Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلاَمُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلاَمُ تَبَارَكْتَ ذَا الْجَلاَلِ وَالإِكْرَامِ
transliteration: Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta ya dhal-jalali wal-ikram.
english_translation: O Allah, You are Peace and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Tu salamti hai aur tujh hi se salamti aati hai. Tu barkat wala hai, ae jalal aur ikram wale!
explanation: Said after seeking forgiveness following the prayer.
context: Thawban reported that after the three istighfars the Prophet ﷺ would say this.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلاَمُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلاَمُ تَبَارَكْتَ ذَا الْجَلاَلِ وَالإِكْرَامِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Glorify, praise and magnify Allah after the prayer
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic:
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ‏.‏
‏{‏الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ‏.‏
لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهْوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ،
transliteration: Subhanallah (33 times). Alhamdulillah (33 times). Allahu akbar (33 times). Then, to complete one hundred: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir.
english_translation: Glory be to Allah. Praise be to Allah. Allah is the Greatest. Then, to complete one hundred: There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things.
roman_urdu_translation: Allah paak hai. Tamam tareef Allah ke liye hai. Allah sab se bada hai. Phir sau poore karne ke liye: Allah ke siwa koi mabood nahin, woh akela hai, uska koi shareek nahin, badshahi usi ki hai, tareef usi ke liye hai aur woh har cheez par qadir hai.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught these words to be said after each obligatory prayer, 33 times each, and completed with the tahlil.
repetition_note: 33 times each for the first three; then the final statement once to make one hundred (Sahih Muslim 597).
context: Poor Muslims came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that the wealthy had greater reward; he taught them this.
arabic_parts: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ‏.‏
‏{‏الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ‏.‏
لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ، وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهْوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ،
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah
narrator: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic:
أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ
لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
wording_note: In this narration the reporter says he believes ('urahu') that the Prophet ﷺ also said the words from 'lahul-mulku' onward. The same phrase 'la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd...' is also reported elsewhere in the Sunnah.
transliteration: Amsayna wa amsal-mulku lillah, walhamdu lillah, la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. Rabbi as'aluka khayra ma fi hadhihil-laylati wa khayra ma ba'daha, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma fi hadhihil-laylati wa sharri ma ba'daha. Rabbi a'udhu bika minal-kasali wa su'il-kibar. Rabbi a'udhu bika min 'adhabin fin-nar, wa 'adhabin fil-qabr.
english_translation: We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and all praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from a punishment in the Fire and a punishment in the grave.
roman_urdu_translation: Hum ne shaam ki aur badshahi Allah ki hui, aur tamam tareef Allah ke liye hai. Allah ke siwa koi mabood nahin, woh akela hai, uska koi shareek nahin, badshahi usi ki hai, tareef usi ke liye hai aur woh har cheez par qadir hai. Ae mere Rab! Main tujh se is raat ki bhalai aur is ke baad ki bhalai mangta hoon, aur is raat ke shar aur is ke baad ke shar se teri panah mangta hoon. Ae mere Rab! Main susti aur budhape ki buri halat se teri panah mangta hoon. Ae mere Rab! Main jahannam ke azaab aur qabr ke azaab se teri panah mangta hoon.
explanation: An evening supplication. It praises Allah, asks for the good of the coming night, and seeks refuge from harm, laziness and punishment.
context: Ibn Mas'ud reported that in the evening the Prophet ﷺ would say this, and in the morning he would say the same beginning with 'Asbahna wa asbahal-mulku lillah'.
arabic_parts: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ

لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Glory be to Allah and with His praise
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
transliteration: Subhanallahi wa bihamdih.
english_translation: Glory be to Allah and with His praise.
roman_urdu_translation: Allah paak hai aur apni tareef ke saath.
explanation: A short phrase of glorification that the Prophet ﷺ encouraged saying in the morning and evening.
repetition_note: The narration specifies 100 times, in the morning and in the evening.
context: Abu Hurayrah reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that whoever says this 100 times in the morning and the evening, no one on the Day of Resurrection will bring anything better than he brought, except one who said the same or more.
arabic_parts: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: When angry: seek refuge in Allah from the accursed devil
narrator: Sulayman ibn Surad (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
transliteration: A'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim.
english_translation: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed devil.
roman_urdu_translation: Main Allah ki panah mangta hoon shaitan mardood se.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ pointed to this phrase as something that, if said, would take away the anger a person feels.
context: Two men were reviling each other in front of the Prophet ﷺ and the face of one reddened with anger; the Prophet ﷺ said that he knew a phrase which, if the man said it, what he felt would leave him — and he named this phrase.
arabic_parts: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Before being with one's spouse: keep Satan away from us
narrator: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ جَنِّبْنَا الشَّيْطَانَ وَجَنِّبِ الشَّيْطَانَ مَا رَزَقْتَنَا‏.‏
transliteration: Bismillah. Allahumma jannibnash-shaytana wa jannibish-shaytana ma razaqtana.
english_translation: In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide for us.
roman_urdu_translation: Allah ke naam se. Ae Allah! Hamein shaitan se door rakh aur jo tu hamein ata kare use bhi shaitan se door rakh.
explanation: A supplication taught for spouses to make before intimacy, seeking Allah's protection for themselves and for what He may grant them.
context: Ibn 'Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught that if one of you says this before approaching his wife, Satan will not harm what Allah decrees.
arabic_parts: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ جَنِّبْنَا الشَّيْطَانَ وَجَنِّبِ الشَّيْطَانَ مَا رَزَقْتَنَا‏.‏
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: In prostration: forgive all my sins
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي كُلَّهُ دِقَّهُ وَجِلَّهُ وَأَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ وَعَلاَنِيَتَهُ وَسِرَّهُ
transliteration: Allahummaghfir li dhanbi kullahu, diqqahu wa jillahu, wa awwalahu wa akhirahu, wa 'alaniyatahu wa sirrah.
english_translation: O Allah, forgive me all my sins — the small and the great, the first and the last, the open and the secret.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Mere tamam gunah bakhsh de, chhote bhi aur bade bhi, pehle bhi aur baad ke bhi, zahir bhi aur posheeda bhi.
explanation: A supplication the Prophet ﷺ made in prostration, covering every category of sin.
context: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to say this in his prostration.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذَنْبِي كُلَّهُ دِقَّهُ وَجِلَّهُ وَأَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ وَعَلاَنِيَتَهُ وَسِرَّهُ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure
narrator: 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعُوذُ بِرِضَاكَ مِنْ سَخَطِكَ وَبِمُعَافَاتِكَ مِنْ عُقُوبَتِكَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْكَ لاَ أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ
transliteration: Allahumma a'udhu biridaka min sakhatik, wa bimu'afatika min 'uqubatik, wa a'udhu bika minka, la uhsi thana'an 'alayk, anta kama athnayta 'ala nafsik.
english_translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count Your praises; You are as You have praised Yourself.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Main teri raza ki panah mangta hoon teri narazgi se, teri maafi ki panah teri saza se, aur main teri panah mangta hoon tujh hi se. Main teri tareef ka shumar nahin kar sakta, tu waisa hi hai jaisa tu ne khud apni tareef ki.
explanation: A prostration supplication that turns to Allah's pleasure and pardon, and admits that His praise cannot be fully counted.
context: 'A'ishah reported that she felt for the Prophet ﷺ in the dark one night and found him prostrating, saying these words.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ أَعُوذُ بِرِضَاكَ مِنْ سَخَطِكَ وَبِمُعَافَاتِكَ مِنْ عُقُوبَتِكَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْكَ لاَ أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Refuge from Hell, the grave, the trials of life and death, and the Dajjal
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ وَمِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
transliteration: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min 'adhabi jahannam, wa min 'adhabil-qabr, wa min fitnatil-mahya wal-mamat, wa min sharri fitnatil-masihid-dajjal.
english_translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the false Messiah.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Main teri panah mangta hoon jahannam ke azaab se, qabr ke azaab se, zindagi aur maut ki aazmaishon se aur masih dajjal ke fitne ke shar se.
explanation: Seeks refuge from four great trials. The Prophet ﷺ taught it for the end of the prayer.
context: Abu Hurayrah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: when one of you finishes the final tashahhud, let him seek refuge in Allah from four things, and he named these.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ وَمِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Guide me to the truth in what they disagree about
narrator: 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ جِبْرَائِيلَ وَمِيكَائِيلَ وَإِسْرَافِيلَ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ اهْدِنِي لِمَا اخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِكَ إِنَّكَ تَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ
transliteration: Allahumma rabba jibra'ila wa mika'ila wa israfil, fatiras-samawati wal-ard, 'alimal-ghaybi wash-shahadah, anta tahkumu bayna 'ibadika fima kanu fihi yakhtalifun. Ihdini lima khtulifa fihi minal-haqqi bi-idhnik, innaka tahdi man tasha'u ila siratin mustaqim.
english_translation: O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You judge between Your servants in what they differ about. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in what is differed upon; You guide whom You will to a straight path.
roman_urdu_translation: Ae Allah! Jibril, Mika'il aur Israfil ke Rab, aasmanon aur zameen ke paida karne wale, ghaib aur zahir ke jaanne wale! Tu apne bandon ke darmiyan un baaton ka faisla karta hai jin mein woh ikhtilaf karte hain. Jis haq mein ikhtilaf kiya gaya, apni ijazat se mujhe uski hidayat de. Beshak tu jise chahe seedhe raste ki hidayat deta hai.
explanation: Asks for guidance to the truth in matters of disagreement and confusion.
context: 'A'ishah was asked with what the Prophet ﷺ opened his night prayer, and she reported that he opened with this.
arabic_parts: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ جِبْرَائِيلَ وَمِيكَائِيلَ وَإِسْرَافِيلَ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ اهْدِنِي لِمَا اخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِكَ إِنَّكَ تَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: The strong person controls themselves when angry
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
transliteration: Laysash-shadidu bis-sur'ah, innamash-shadidul-ladhi yamliku nafsahu 'indal-ghadab.
english_translation: The strong person is not the one who defeats others in wrestling; the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry.
roman_urdu_translation: Taqatwar woh nahin jo kushti mein doosron ko pachhaad de, taqatwar woh hai jo gusse ke waqt apne aap par qaboo rakhe.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ redefines strength as self-control in a moment of anger.
arabic_parts: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Do not become angry
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: لاَ تَغْضَبُ
transliteration: La taghdab.
english_translation: Do not become angry.
roman_urdu_translation: Gussa na kiya karo.
explanation: The advice the Prophet ﷺ gave, and repeated, to a man who asked for counsel.
context: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice. The Prophet ﷺ said 'Do not become angry', and the man asked again several times; each time the Prophet ﷺ repeated the same words.
arabic_parts: لاَ تَغْضَبُ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: The closest a servant is to their Lord is in prostration
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَكْثِرُوا الدُّعَاءَ
transliteration: Aqrabu ma yakunul-'abdu min rabbihi wa huwa sajid, fa akthirud-du'a'.
english_translation: The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make abundant supplication.
roman_urdu_translation: Banda apne Rab ke sab se zyada qareeb sajde ki halat mein hota hai, pas us mein bohat dua kiya karo.
explanation: An invitation to pour out one's requests in prostration.
arabic_parts: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ فَأَكْثِرُوا الدُّعَاءَ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: Every disease has a cure
narrator: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
arabic: لِكُلِّ دَاءٍ دَوَاءٌ فَإِذَا أُصِيبَ دَوَاءُ الدَّاءِ بَرَأَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
transliteration: Likulli da'in dawa', fa idha usiba dawa'ud-da'i bara'a bi-idhnillahi 'azza wa jall.
english_translation: Every disease has a cure. When the cure is found for the disease, it is healed by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
roman_urdu_translation: Har bimari ki dawa hai. Jab bimari ko uski dawa pahunch jaye to Allah ke hukm se shifa ho jati hai.
explanation: Seeking treatment is part of the Prophet's ﷺ teaching. This applies to physical illness and, in our time, to mental health care as well.
arabic_parts: لِكُلِّ دَاءٍ دَوَاءٌ فَإِذَا أُصِيبَ دَوَاءُ الدَّاءِ بَرَأَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: The affair of the believer is all good
narrator: Suhayb ibn Sinan (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: عَجَبًا لأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَلَيْسَ ذَاكَ لأَحَدٍ إِلاَّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ إِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ سَرَّاءُ شَكَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ ضَرَّاءُ صَبَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ
transliteration: 'Ajaban li-amril-mu'min, inna amrahu kullahu khayr, wa laysa dhaka li-ahadin illa lil-mu'min. In asabat-hu sarra'u shakara fakana khayran lah, wa in asabat-hu darra'u sabara fakana khayran lah.
english_translation: How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good, and this is only for the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him. If something harmful happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.
roman_urdu_translation: Momin ka muamla bhi ajeeb hai, uske liye har haal mein bhalai hai, aur yeh sirf momin ke liye hai. Agar usay khushi pahunche to shukr karta hai aur yeh uske liye behtar hai, aur agar takleef pahunche to sabr karta hai aur yeh bhi uske liye behtar hai.
explanation: Both gratitude in ease and patience in hardship are described as good for the believer.
arabic_parts: عَجَبًا لأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَلَيْسَ ذَاكَ لأَحَدٍ إِلاَّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ إِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ سَرَّاءُ شَكَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ ضَرَّاءُ صَبَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ
grading_source: Reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and/or Sahih Muslim, the two collections whose compilers set authenticity as a condition of inclusion.

title: No worry or grief touches a believer without it counting for them
narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them)
arabic: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حُزْنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى وَلاَ غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا، إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ
transliteration: Ma yusibul-muslima min nasabin wa la wasabin wa la hammin wa la huznin wa la adhan wa la ghammin hattash-shawkati yushakuha illa kaffarallahu biha min khataya'h.
english_translation: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm or distress befalls a Muslim — even the prick of a thorn — except that Allah expiates some of his sins because of it.
roman_urdu_translation: Musalman ko jo bhi thakan, bimari, fikr, gham, takleef ya pareshani pahunchti hai, yahan tak ke kaanta bhi chubhta hai, Allah us ke badle us ke gunahon mein se kuch maaf kar deta hai.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ names worry and grief explicitly. Your pain is seen, and it is not wasted. This does not say that you should not seek relief or help.
arabic_parts: مَا يُصِيبُ الْمُسْلِمَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ وَلاَ هَمٍّ وَلاَ حُزْنٍ وَلاَ أَذًى وَلاَ غَمٍّ حَتَّى الشَّوْكَةِ يُشَاكُهَا، إِلاَّ كَفَّرَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ خَطَايَاهُ

title: True patience is at the first shock
narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إِنَّمَا الصَّبْرُ عِنْدَ الصَّدْمَةِ الأُولَى
transliteration: Innamas-sabru 'indas-sadmatil-ula.
english_translation: Patience is only at the first shock.
roman_urdu_translation: Sabr to pehle sadme ke waqt hi hai.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said this to a woman who was crying at a grave. It points to the first moment of loss as the place where patience matters most.
context: He passed a woman weeping at a grave and told her to fear Allah and be patient. She did not recognise him and answered sharply; when she learned who he was, she came to him and he said these words.
arabic_parts: إِنَّمَا الصَّبْرُ عِنْدَ الصَّدْمَةِ الأُولَى

title: Do not say 'if only' — say 'Allah decreed, and what He willed, He did'
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلاَ تَعْجِزْ وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَىْءٌ فَلاَ تَقُلْ لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏.‏ وَلَكِنْ قُلْ قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ
transliteration: Al-mu'minul-qawiyyu khayrun wa ahabbu ilallahi minal-mu'minid-da'if, wa fi kullin khayr. Ihris 'ala ma yanfa'uk, wasta'in billahi wa la ta'jiz. Wa in asabaka shay'un fala taqul: law anni fa'altu kana kadha wa kadha, wa lakin qul: qaddarallahu wa ma sha'a fa'al, fa inna law taftahu 'amalash-shaytan.
english_translation: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so-and-so.' Rather say: 'Allah has decreed, and what He willed, He did.' For 'if only' opens the door to the work of Satan.
roman_urdu_translation: Taqatwar momin Allah ke nazdeek kamzor momin se behtar aur zyada pasandeeda hai, aur dono mein bhalai hai. Us cheez ki koshish karo jo tumhein nafa de, Allah se madad mango aur himmat na haaro. Agar tumhein koi museebat pahunche to yeh na kaho ke agar main aisa kar leta to aisa ho jata, balke kaho: Allah ne muqaddar kiya aur jo us ne chaha kiya, kyunke 'agar' shaitan ke kaam ka darwaza kholta hai.
explanation: Advice for the mind that keeps replaying what could have been done differently: act on what you can, ask Allah for help, and leave what has passed with Allah's decree.
arabic_parts: الْمُؤْمِنُ الْقَوِيُّ خَيْرٌ وَأَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ الضَّعِيفِ وَفِي كُلٍّ خَيْرٌ احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلاَ تَعْجِزْ وَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَىْءٌ فَلاَ تَقُلْ لَوْ أَنِّي فَعَلْتُ كَانَ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏.‏ وَلَكِنْ قُلْ قَدَرُ اللَّهِ وَمَا شَاءَ فَعَلَ فَإِنَّ لَوْ تَفْتَحُ عَمَلَ الشَّيْطَانِ

title: Your self has a right over you
narrator: Abu Juhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إِنَّ لِرَبِّكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَلِنَفْسِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَلأَهْلِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، فَأَعْطِ كُلَّ ذِي حَقٍّ حَقَّهُ‏.‏
transliteration: Inna lirabbika 'alayka haqqan, wa linafsika 'alayka haqqan, wa li-ahlika 'alayka haqqan, fa a'ti kulla dhi haqqin haqqah.
english_translation: Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each its due.
roman_urdu_translation: Tere Rab ka tujh par haq hai, tere nafs ka tujh par haq hai aur tere ghar walon ka tujh par haq hai, pas har haq wale ko uska haq ada kar.
explanation: Rest and care for oneself are named as a right alongside worship and family.
context: Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him) said this to his brother Abu ad-Darda', who was fasting and praying through the nights and neglecting his family. When the Prophet ﷺ heard it, he said: 'Salman has spoken the truth.'
arabic_parts: إِنَّ لِرَبِّكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَلِنَفْسِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، وَلأَهْلِكَ عَلَيْكَ حَقًّا، فَأَعْطِ كُلَّ ذِي حَقٍّ حَقَّهُ‏.‏

title: The religion is ease
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ، فَسَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا وَأَبْشِرُوا،
transliteration: Innad-dina yusr, wa lan yushaddad-dina ahadun illa ghalabah. Fa saddidu wa qaribu wa abshiru.
english_translation: Indeed the religion is ease, and no one makes the religion difficult for themselves except that it overcomes them. So be moderate, strive to do what you can, and have good hope.
roman_urdu_translation: Beshak deen aasani hai, aur jo koi deen ko apne upar sakht kar le to woh us par ghalib aa jata hai. Pas meana ravi ikhtiyar karo, durustgi ki koshish karo aur khush khabri lo.
explanation: A reminder to approach worship and effort steadily and without exhausting oneself.
arabic_parts: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ، وَلَنْ يُشَادَّ الدِّينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ، فَسَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا وَأَبْشِرُوا،

title: The eye weeps and the heart grieves
narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إِنَّ الْعَيْنَ تَدْمَعُ، وَالْقَلْبَ يَحْزَنُ، وَلاَ نَقُولُ إِلاَّ مَا يَرْضَى رَبُّنَا، وَإِنَّا بِفِرَاقِكَ يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ لَمَحْزُونُونَ
transliteration: Innal-'ayna tadma'u wal-qalba yahzanu wa la naqulu illa ma yarda rabbuna, wa inna bifiraqika ya Ibrahimu lamahzunun.
english_translation: The eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. O Ibrahim, we are grieved at your departure.
roman_urdu_translation: Aankh aansu bahati hai aur dil ghamgeen hota hai, aur hum wohi kehte hain jis se hamara Rab razi ho. Ae Ibrahim! Hum tere bichhadne par ghamgeen hain.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ's own words when his young son died. Grief and tears are natural and are not a failure of faith.
context: The Prophet ﷺ said this at the death of his son Ibrahim, while his eyes were shedding tears.
arabic_parts: إِنَّ الْعَيْنَ تَدْمَعُ، وَالْقَلْبَ يَحْزَنُ، وَلاَ نَقُولُ إِلاَّ مَا يَرْضَى رَبُّنَا، وَإِنَّا بِفِرَاقِكَ يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ لَمَحْزُونُونَ

title: I am as My servant thinks of Me
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أَنَا عِنْدَ ظَنِّ عَبْدِي بِي، وَأَنَا مَعَهُ إِذَا ذَكَرَنِي،
transliteration: Ana 'inda zanni 'abdi bi, wa ana ma'ahu idha dhakarani.
english_translation: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.
roman_urdu_translation: Main apne bande ke gumaan ke mutabiq hoon jo woh mere bare mein rakhta hai, aur main us ke saath hoon jab woh mujhe yaad karta hai.
explanation: A hadith qudsi: words that the Prophet ﷺ reported from Allah. It invites a hopeful view of Allah and describes His company with those who remember Him.

title: My mercy prevails over My wrath
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إِنَّ رَحْمَتِي سَبَقَتْ غَضَبِي
transliteration: Inna rahmati sabaqat ghadabi.
english_translation: Indeed, My mercy has preceded My wrath.
roman_urdu_translation: Beshak meri rehmat mere ghazab par sabqat le gayi.
explanation: A hadith qudsi: Allah wrote this for Himself when He created the creation. Wordings differ slightly between narrations (e.g. 'prevails over' and 'precedes').
context: The Prophet ﷺ said: when Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy precedes My wrath.'

title: Entering the home: mention Allah
narrator: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
arabic: إِذَا دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ بَيْتَهُ فَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَ دُخُولِهِ وَعِنْدَ طَعَامِهِ قَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ لاَ مَبِيتَ لَكُمْ وَلاَ عَشَاءَ
transliteration: Idha dakhalar-rajulu baytahu fadhakarallaha 'inda dukhulihi wa 'inda ta'amihi qalash-shaytanu la mabita lakum wa la 'asha'.
english_translation: When a man enters his house and mentions Allah upon entering and while eating, Satan says: 'You have no place to spend the night and no supper.'
roman_urdu_translation: Jab aadmi apne ghar mein dakhil hota hai aur dakhil hote waqt aur khana khate waqt Allah ka zikr karta hai to shaitan kehta hai: tumhare liye na yahan raat guzarne ki jagah hai na raat ka khana.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged mentioning Allah's name on entering the home. A specific wording from other narrations is under review in this collection.
arabic_parts: إِذَا دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ بَيْتَهُ فَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَ دُخُولِهِ وَعِنْدَ طَعَامِهِ قَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ لاَ مَبِيتَ لَكُمْ وَلاَ عَشَاءَ
